inputs.text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. That is a serious breach, not merely a stunt—and it shows why election rules must be secure and consistently enforced. The reflex to warn that discussing vulnerabilities will undermine trust is backwards: public confidence depends on taking real weaknesses seriously, not treating scrutiny as suspect. Protecting the vote and preserving fair access should go together, but access cannot mean looking away when someone tries to obtain another person’s ballot.
